Synopsis:
A reflationist adviser to Japan's PM Takaichi projects the BOJ will hike rates at its September 17-18 meeting to 1.25%, followed by another hike by January 2026, then reverting to a pace of roughly once every six months. The window for a September hike is driven partly by parliamentary timing. US Treasury Secretary Bessent's public calls for higher BOJ rates and BOJ Governor Ueda's open signalling have reinforced market pricing, which now nearly fully reflects a 25bps hike this month. The article highlights growing consensus within even the dovish Takaichi administration that further BOJ tightening is needed to stabilise the yen.
